- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.10) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.20) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Lag in correction: model often overreacts to recent spikes, then undercorrects in subsequent days — apply smoothing or delay adjustment for 2–3 day horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently holds prices too high after strong upward moves — reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 day horizons post-spike.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term sentiment momentum — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for longer horizons if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is neutral or trending sideways, model often overreacts — cap forecast deviation to ±1.5% of recent 7-day average.
